events.title: Swahili-Arab slave trade at Nkhotakota
hints: A lakeshore town became the main collection point for captives heading to the Indian Ocean coast.
Its ruler, known as the Jumbe, was a Swahili-Arab trader linked to a sultan on an island off the coast.
David Livingstone visited and campaigned against the trade.
events.summary: From the 1840s the lakeshore town of Nkhotakota, then Kota Kota, was a major collection point for enslaved people sent to the Indian Ocean coast, run by a Swahili-Arab ruler known as the Jumbe with links to Zanzibar. British forces ended the trade there in the 1890s.

events.title: British Central Africa Protectorate and Nyasaland
hints: Britain declared a protectorate in 1891 after clashes with Portugal over the lake region.
European-owned estates took much of the best land in the south.
Tobacco, tea and cotton were the main exports.
events.summary: Britain declared the British Central Africa Protectorate in 1891, renamed Nyasaland in 1907. European-owned estates took much of the best land in the south, and tobacco, tea and cotton were the main exports. Independence came in 1964.

events.title: Thangata labour tenancy
hints: On European estates, African tenants had to work for the landowner in return for the right to stay on land.
The word once meant neighbourly help but came to describe an exploitative labour-rent system.
Tenants who refused could be evicted, and the system was abolished in 1962.
events.summary: Under the thangata system on European estates, Africans who lived on estate land had to work for the owner in lieu of rent. A traditional term for reciprocal help took on a coercive meaning, and the system was a source of grievances until its abolition in 1962.

events.title: Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland
territoryNames: the Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland
hints: Britain joined three territories into a federation in 1953 over the objections of most Africans.
Revenue from copper mines in the middle territory helped fund development in the south.
This territory supplied migrant workers to its richer partners.
events.summary: In 1953 Britain created the Central African Federation from Southern Rhodesia, Northern Rhodesia and Nyasaland despite African opposition. Copper revenues from the north largely benefited the south, and Nyasaland served as a labour reserve. The federation collapsed in 1963.
events.quip: A federation imposed over local objections lasted ten years, which was about nine years longer than it deserved.
